summary: This special election filled the rest of a term for a seat vacated when JD Vance became Vice President. Sherrod Brown (Democrat) defeated Jon Husted (Republican), who had been appointed to the seat.

candidates.name: Sherrod Brown
candidates.bio: Sherrod Brown served as a U.S. senator from Ohio from 2007 to 2025, and earlier as Ohio Secretary of State and in the U.S. House. He chaired the Senate Banking Committee.

positions.summary: Says affordability is his central theme and argues trade policy should protect domestic manufacturing and workers' bargaining power.
Says he supports reversing federal Medicaid cuts, lowering prescription drug prices and preventing insurers from denying medically necessary care.
Says he wants a stronger border with more resources for border agents, and voted to speed up asylum claims.
Opposes public funding for private and for-profit schools, saying vouchers divert money from public education.
Voted for $369 billion in clean energy tax credits.
Says abortion decisions are "intensely personal" and should be made by women and their doctors.

candidates.name: Jon Husted
candidates.bio: Jon Husted was appointed to the U.S. Senate in January 2025 to fill the seat vacated by JD Vance. He previously served as Ohio lieutenant governor (from 2019), secretary of state (2011-2019) and speaker of the Ohio House.

positions.summary: His campaign says he was proud to pass the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, which it says eliminated taxes on tips, overtime and Social Security.
Voted against extending the Affordable Care Act tax credits and has called the ACA dysfunctional.
His campaign says he is committed to keeping the border secure and is fighting for Ohioans, "not people in our country illegally."
Supports school choice, including tax credits for faith-based education, and says he helped create Ohio's EdChoice scholarship.
Says Brown's "radical climate change agenda" shut 23 power plants in Ohio, and says he has legislation to require data centers to build their own power.
His campaign biography calls him a "champion for life."

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35); also confirmed by news5cleveland.com report. Shares taken Nov. 25, 2026 from The Green Papers, unofficial, with write-ins in the total. State certification was not confirmed.
